units.zh: 翟光鄴
units.en: Zhai Guangye
units.literal: Zhai Guangye

units.zh: 翟光鄴，字化基，濮州鄄城人也。
units.en: Zhai Guangye, styled Huaji, came from Juancheng in Puzhou.
units.literal: Zhai Guangye, courtesy name Huaji, was a native of Juancheng in Puzhou.

units.zh: 其父景珂，倜儻有膽氣。
units.en: His father Jing Ke was a man of dash and nerve.
units.literal: His father Jing Ke was bold and daring.

units.zh: 梁、晉相距於河上，景珂率聚邑人守永定驛，晉人攻之，逾年不能下，景珂卒戰死。
units.en: Liang and Jin faced off on the river. Jing Ke rallied the townsmen to hold Yongding Post. Jin besieged it a year and could not break it; Jing Ke fell in the last fight.
units.literal: When Liang and Jin faced each other on the Yellow River, Jing Ke led the assembled townspeople to hold Yongding Post. Jin forces attacked for more than a year without taking it; Jing Ke died fighting in the end.

units.zh: 光鄴時年十歲，為晉兵所掠，明宗愛其穎悟，常以自隨。
units.en: Guangye was ten when Jin soldiers carried him off. Mingzong prized his sharp mind and kept him close.
units.literal: Guangye was then ten years old, carried off by Jin troops; Mingzong loved his quick wit and always kept him at his side.

units.zh: 光鄴事唐，官至耀州團練使。
units.en: Under Tang he rose to training commissioner of Yao.
units.literal: Guangye served Tang and rose to training commissioner of Yaozhou.

units.zh: 晉高祖時，歷棣沂二州刺史、西京副留守。
units.en: Under Jin Gaozu he was prefect of Di and Yi in turn and deputy defender of the Western Capital.
units.literal: Under Jin Gaozu he successively held the prefectures of Di and Yi and was deputy defender of the Western Capital.

units.zh: 出帝已破楊光遠，以光鄴為青州防禦使。
units.en: Once the Deposed Emperor had broken Yang Guangyuan, Guangye was made defender of Qing.
units.literal: After the Deposed Emperor had defeated Yang Guangyuan, Guangye was made defender of Qingzhou.

units.zh: 光鄴招輯兵民，甚有恩意。
units.en: Guangye rallied troops and civilians with real grace.
units.literal: Guangye gathered soldiers and people with great kindness.

units.zh: 契丹滅晉，遣光鄴知曹州。
units.en: When the Khitan ended Jin, they set Guangye to govern Cao.
units.literal: When the Khitan destroyed Jin, they sent Guangye to govern Caozhou.

units.zh: 許王從益入汴，以為樞密使。
units.en: When Prince Xu Congyi entered Bian, he was made Privy Commissioner.
units.literal: When Prince Xu Congyi entered Bian, Guangye was made Privy Commissioner.

units.zh: 漢高祖入京師，改右領軍衛大將軍、左金吾大將軍，充街使。
units.en: Han Gaozu entered the capital and made him Grand General of the Right Stern Guard and Grand General of the Left Jinwu Guard, and street commissioner.
units.literal: When Han Gaozu entered the capital, Guangye was changed to Grand General of the Right Stern Guard and Grand General of the Left Golden Crow, and served as street commissioner.

units.zh: 周太祖入立，拜宣徽使、樞密副使，出知永興軍，卒於官。
units.en: Zhou Taizu took the throne and named him Palace Commissioner and Vice Privy Commissioner, then sent him to govern Yongxing; he died in post.
units.literal: When Zhou Taizu took the throne, Guangye was appointed Palace Commissioner and Vice Privy Commissioner, then sent out to govern Yongxing army and died in office.

units.zh: 光鄴為人沈默多謀，事繼母以孝聞。
units.en: Guangye spoke little and plotted much, and was known for honoring his stepmother.
units.literal: Guangye was a man of few words and many plans, famed for filial devotion to his stepmother.

units.zh: 雖貴，不營財產，常假官舍以居，蕭然僅蔽風雨。
units.en: Though high in rank he built no fortune, lodging in borrowed government rooms, spare enough only to shed wind and rain.
units.literal: Though ennobled, he did not amass property, often borrowing official quarters to live in, bare enough only to keep off wind and rain.

units.zh: 雍睦親族，粗衣糲食，與均有無，而光鄴處之晏然，日與賓客飲酒聚書為樂。
units.en: He kept kin close in coarse dress and plain fare, sharing all he had while he stayed easy, drinking with guests and piling books for joy.
units.literal: He was harmonious with his kin, wore coarse clothes and ate plain food, sharing what he had with them, while Guangye himself remained at ease, daily drinking with guests and gathering books for pleasure.

units.zh: 其所臨政，務以寬靜休息為意。
units.en: Wherever he ruled, he aimed at leniency, quiet, and ease.
units.literal: In every post he governed, his aim was leniency, quiet, and rest.

units.zh: 病亟，戒其左右，氣絕以屍歸洛，無久留以煩軍府。
units.en: Near death he told his men: when breath fails, bear my body to Luoyang—do not linger and burden the command.
units.literal: When his illness grew urgent he warned his attendants: when breath failed, carry the corpse back to Luoyang—do not linger and trouble the army headquarters.

units.zh: 既卒，州人上書乞留葬立祠，不許。
units.en: After his death the prefecture petitioned to bury him locally and raise a shrine; the court refused.
units.literal: After he died the people of the prefecture petitioned to bury him there and raise a shrine; the court refused.

units.zh: 馮暉，魏州人也。
units.en: Feng Hui came from Weizhou.
units.literal: Feng Hui was a native of Weizhou.

units.zh: 為效節軍卒，以功遷隊長。
units.en: He served the Loyalty army as a soldier and rose to squad leader by merit.
units.literal: He was a soldier of the Loyalty army and, by merit, was promoted to squad leader.

units.zh: 唐莊宗入魏，與梁相距於河上，暉以隊長亡入梁軍，王彥章以暉驍勇，隸之麾下。
units.en: Zhuangzong entered Wei and faced Liang on the river. Hui fled from his squad into Liang ranks. Wang Yanzhang took his dash and kept him close.
units.literal: When Tang’s Zhuangzong entered Wei and faced Liang on the river, Hui as squad leader fled into the Liang army; Wang Yanzhang, finding Hui fierce and brave, placed him under his command.

units.zh: 梁亡，莊宗赦暉不問。
units.en: Liang fell; Zhuangzong pardoned Hui and let the matter drop.
units.literal: When Liang fell, Zhuangzong pardoned Hui and did not pursue the matter.

units.zh: 從明宗討楊立、魏王繼岌平蜀，累遷夔、興二州刺史。
units.en: He followed Mingzong against Yang Li and joined the Prince of Wei Jiji in pacifying Shu, rising to prefect of Kui and Xing.
units.literal: He followed Mingzong against Yang Li and the Prince of Wei Jiji in pacifying Shu, and was repeatedly promoted to prefect of Qiong and Xing.

units.zh: 董璋反東川，暉從晉高祖討璋，軍至劍門，劍門兵守，不得入，暉從佗道出其左，擊蜀守兵殆盡。
units.en: Dong Zhang rebelled in Dongchuan. Hui marched with Jin Gaozu to Jianmen, which held shut. He swung left by another road and cut down the Shu garrison almost to a man.
units.literal: When Dong Zhang rebelled in Dongchuan, Hui followed Jin Gaozu to attack Zhang. The army reached Jianmen; Jianmen’s garrison held and they could not enter. Hui took another road out to its left and struck the Shu defenders until nearly all were gone.

units.zh: 會晉高祖班師，拜暉澶州刺史。
units.en: Gaozu withdrew and made Hui prefect of Chan.
units.literal: When Jin Gaozu withdrew the army, Hui was made prefect of Chan.

units.zh: 天福中，範延光反魏州，遣暉襲滑州，不克，遂入於魏，為延光守。
units.en: Under Tianfu, Fan Yanguang rebelled at Wei and sent Hui against Hua. Hui failed, entered Wei, and held it for Yanguang.
units.literal: In the Tianfu era Fan Yanguang rebelled at Weizhou and sent Hui to strike Hua prefecture. He could not take it, then entered Wei and held it for Yanguang.

units.zh: 已而出降，拜義成軍節度使，徙鎮靈武。
units.en: Soon he surrendered, was made commissioner of Yicheng, and was shifted to Lingwu.
units.literal: Before long he came out and surrendered, was made military commissioner of the Yicheng army, and was transferred to govern Lingwu.

units.zh: 靈武自唐明宗已後，市馬糴粟，招來部族，給賜軍士，歲用度支錢六千萬，自關以西，轉輸供給，民不堪役，而流亡甚眾。
units.en: Since Mingzong, Lingwu had traded for horses and grain, drawn tribes in, and paid the troops—sixty million a year from the treasury. West of the Pass the convoys broke the people, and exiles swarmed.
units.literal: Since Tang’s Mingzong, Lingwu had bought horses and grain, drawn in tribal groups, and paid out to the soldiers—sixty million strings from the treasury each year. West of the Pass the transport supply wore the people out, and exiles were very many.

units.zh: 青岡、土橋之間，氐、羌剽掠道路，商旅行必以兵。
units.en: Between Qinggang and Tuqiao, Di and Qiang robbed the roads, and merchants marched only under arms.
units.literal: Between Qinggang and Tuqiao, Di and Qiang plundered the roads, and merchants had to travel with armed escort.

units.zh: 暉始至，則推以恩信，部族懷惠，止息侵奪，然後廣屯田以省轉餉，治倉庫、亭館千餘區，多出俸錢，民不加賦，管內大治，晉高祖下詔書褒美。
units.en: Hui came and ruled by grace and trust; the tribes took his favor and raids stopped. He widened garrison farms to spare the convoys, raised a thousand storehouses and lodges from his own pay without new levies, and brought the circuit to order. Jin Gaozu praised him by edict.
units.literal: When Hui first arrived he won them with kindness and trust; the tribes felt his grace and raids ceased. Then he expanded garrison farming to cut transport costs, built more than a thousand storehouses and lodges, spending mostly from his own salary so the people paid no new levies. Within his circuit there was great order, and Jin Gaozu issued an edict of praise.

units.zh: 党項拓拔彥超最為大族，諸族向背常以彥超為去就。
units.en: Of the Tangut, Tuoba Yanchao was the greatest house; tribes turned or held by his lead.
units.literal: Among the Tangut, Tuoba Yanchao was the greatest clan; whether tribes turned or held back usually followed Yanchao.

units.zh: 暉之至也，彥超來謁，遂留之，為起第於城中，賜予豐厚，務足其意。
units.en: Yanchao came to call. Hui kept him, built him a house in the city, and heaped gifts until he was content.
units.literal: When Hui arrived Yanchao came to call on him. Hui detained him, built him a mansion in the city, and gave lavish gifts to satisfy his wishes.

units.zh: 彥超既留，而諸部族爭以羊馬為市易，期年有馬五千匹。
units.en: With Yanchao held, tribes traded sheep and horses in rivalry; within a year Hui had five thousand horses.
units.literal: Once Yanchao was detained, the tribes vied to trade sheep and horses; within a year there were five thousand horses.

units.zh: 晉見暉馬多而得夷心，反以為患，徙鎮靜難，又徙保義。
units.en: Jin saw his horses and tribal favor and took alarm; he was moved to Jingnan, then to Baoyi.
units.literal: Jin saw that Hui had many horses and had won the tribes’ hearts, and instead took it as a worry; he was transferred to govern Jingnan, then again to Baoyi.

units.zh: 歲中，召為侍衛步軍都指揮使，領河陽節度使，暉於是始覺晉有患己意。
units.en: That year he was recalled as Palace Foot Guard commander with He-Yang; Hui first felt Jin’s mistrust.
units.literal: Within the year he was summoned as commander of the Palace Foot Guard and held the He-Yang military commission; Hui then first sensed that Jin meant him harm.

units.zh: 是時，出帝昏亂，馮玉、李彥韜等用事，暉曲意事之，因得復鎮靈武。
units.en: The Deposed Emperor was lost; Feng Yu and Li Yantao held court. Hui courted them and won Lingwu back.
units.literal: At that time the Deposed Emperor was muddled; Feng Yu, Li Yantao, and others held power. Hui bent his will to serve them and thereby regained Lingwu.

units.zh: 時王令溫鎮靈武，失夷落心，大為邊患。
units.en: Wang Lingwen held Lingwu, lost the tribes, and bred great border trouble.
units.literal: Wang Lingwen then governed Lingwu, lost the tribes’ hearts, and became a great border trouble.

units.zh: 暉即請曰：「今朝廷多事，必不能以兵援臣，願得自募兵以為衛。」
units.en: Hui petitioned at once: "The court is beset and cannot send you troops. Let me raise my own guard."
units.literal: Hui at once petitioned, saying: "The court now has many troubles and surely cannot send troops to aid your subject. I beg leave to raise troops myself for guard."

units.zh: 乃募得兵千餘人，行至梅戍，蕃夷稍稍來謁，暉顧首領一人，指其佩劍曰：「此板橋王氏劍邪？
units.en: He raised a thousand-odd men. At Mei garrison tribesmen called in turn. Hui eyed one chief, pointed at his belt sword, and said: "A Banqiao Wang blade?
units.literal: He then raised more than a thousand troops. Reaching Mei garrison, tribesmen came to call one after another. Hui glanced at one chieftain, pointed at the sword at his belt, and said: "Is this a Banqiao Wang blade?

units.zh: 吾聞王氏劍天下利器也。」
units.en: I hear Wang blades are the finest steel under heaven."
units.literal: I have heard the Wang blade is the finest weapon under heaven."

units.zh: 俯而取諸腰間，若將玩之，因擊殺首領者，其從騎十餘人皆殺之。
units.en: He bent as if to admire it, took it from the man’s belt, and killed the chief and a dozen of his riders besides.
units.literal: He bent and took it from the man’s waist as if to admire it, then struck and killed the chieftain, and killed more than ten of his mounted followers as well.

units.zh: 裨將藥元福曰：「今去靈武尚五六百里，奈何？」
units.en: Deputy Yao Yuanfu said: "Lingwu is still five or six hundred li off—what now?"
units.literal: Deputy Yao Yuanfu said: "We are still five or six hundred li from Lingwu—what then?"

units.zh: 暉笑曰：「此夷落之豪，部族之所恃也，吾能殺之，其餘豈敢動哉！」
units.en: Hui laughed: "This was their great chief, the tribes’ pillar. Kill him and who dares move?"
units.literal: Hui laughed and said: "This is a chieftain of the tribes, the one the clans rely on. If I can kill him, how would the rest dare stir!"

units.zh: 已而諸族皆以兵扼道路，暉以言譬諭之，獨所殺首領一族求戰，即與之戰而敗走，諸族遂不敢動。
units.en: Soon every tribe barred the road. Hui talked them down; only the dead chief’s clan fought. He beat them off, and the rest held still.
units.literal: Before long every tribe took up arms to block the road. Hui reasoned with them in words; only the clan of the slain chieftain sought battle. He fought them, they were beaten and fled, and the tribes then dared not move.

units.zh: 暉至靈武，撫綏邊部，凡十餘年，恩信大著。
units.en: At Lingwu he soothed the border tribes more than ten years until grace and trust shone wide.
units.literal: Hui reached Lingwu and soothed the border tribes for more than ten years; his kindness and trust became greatly renowned.

units.zh: 官至中書令，封陳留王。
units.en: He rose to Grand Councilor and was enfeoffed Prince of Chenliu.
units.literal: He rose to Grand Councilor and was enfeoffed as Prince of Chenliu.

units.zh: 廣順三年卒，追封衛王。
units.en: He died in the third year of Guangshun and was posthumously made Prince of Wei.
units.literal: In the third year of Guangshun he died; posthumously he was enfeoffed as Prince of Wei.

units.zh: 子繼業。
units.en: He left a son Jiye.
units.literal: He had a son Jiye.

units.zh: 皇甫暉
units.en: Huang Fuhui
units.literal: Huang Fuhui

units.zh: 皇甫暉，魏州人也。
units.en: Huang Fuhui came from Weizhou.
units.literal: Huang Fuhui was a native of Weizhou.

units.zh: 為魏軍卒，戍瓦橋關，歲滿當代歸，而留屯貝州。
units.en: He was a Wei soldier at Waqiao Pass. His term ended and he should have gone home, but the army kept him at Bei.
units.literal: He was a Wei soldier, garrisoned at Waqiao Pass; when his term ended he should have been relieved and sent home, but instead was left to garrison at Bei prefecture.

units.zh: 是時，唐莊宗已失政，天下離心。
units.en: Zhuangzong had already lost the realm, and hearts everywhere pulled apart.
units.literal: At that time Tang’s Zhuangzong had already lost good government, and the realm’s hearts were divided.

units.zh: 暉為人驍勇無賴，夜博軍中，不勝，乃與其徒謀為亂，劫其部將楊仁晟曰：「唐能破梁而得天下者，以先得魏而盡有河北兵也。
units.en: Fuhui was brutal and reckless. He gambled in camp at night, lost, and with his mates plotted mutiny. They seized their officer Yang Rencheng and said: "Tang broke Liang because it took Wei first and held all Hebei arms.
units.literal: Fuhui was fierce and lawless. He gambled in camp at night, lost, and with his fellows plotted mutiny. They seized their commander Yang Rencheng and said: "Tang could break Liang and take the realm because it first took Wei and thereby held all the Hebei armies.

units.zh: 魏軍甲不去體、馬不解鞍者十餘年，今天下已定，而天子不念魏軍久戍之勞，去家咫尺，不得相見。
units.en: For ten years Wei men never stripped mail or ungirt saddles. The realm is settled, yet the throne forgets our long watch. Home is a step away and we cannot see kin.
units.literal: Wei soldiers for more than ten years did not remove armor from their bodies or saddles from their horses. Now the realm is settled, yet the Son of Heaven does not remember the Wei army’s long garrison toil. Home is a foot away, yet they cannot see their kin.

units.zh: 今將士思歸不可遏，公當與我俱行。
units.en: Our longing to return cannot be held. March with us.
units.literal: The soldiers’ longing to return cannot be stopped. You must march with us.

units.zh: 不幸天子怒吾軍，則坐據一州，足以起事。」
units.en: If the throne rages at us, seize a prefecture and that is enough to rise."
units.literal: If the Son of Heaven should rage at our army, then sit and hold one prefecture—enough to raise an affair."

units.zh: 仁晟曰：「公等何計之過也！
units.en: Rencheng said: "Your plans go too far!
units.literal: Rencheng said: "Your plans go too far!

units.zh: 今英主在上，天下一家，精甲銳兵，不下數十萬，公等各有家屬，何故出此不祥之言？」
units.en: A bright lord rules, the realm is one house, and sharp arms number in the hundreds of thousands. You have kin—why such ill-omened talk?"
units.literal: A brilliant lord sits above, the realm is one house, and keen armor and sharp weapons number no less than several hundred thousand. You each have families—why speak such ill-omened words?"

units.zh: 軍士知不可強，遂斬之，推一小校為主，不從，又斬之，乃攜二首以詣裨將趙在禮，在禮從之，乃夜焚貝州以入於魏，在禮以暉為馬步軍都指揮使。
units.en: The soldiers knew they could not force him, so they beheaded him; they pushed a junior officer to be leader, he refused, and they beheaded him too. Carrying the two heads they went to deputy Zhao Zaili; Zaili followed them. That night they burned Bei and entered Wei; Zaili made Fuhui horse-and-foot commander.
units.literal: They pushed a junior officer to be leader; he would not obey, and they beheaded him too. Then carrying the two heads they went to deputy Zhao Zaili; Zaili followed them. That night they burned Bei prefecture and entered Wei; Zaili made Fuhui commander of the horse and foot army.

units.zh: 暉擁甲士數百騎，大掠城中，至一民家，問其姓，曰：「姓國。」
units.en: Fuhui led hundreds of armored horse and plundered the city. At one house he asked the surname; they said: "Guo."
units.literal: Fuhui led several hundred armored horsemen and plundered greatly through the city. At one household he asked the surname; they said: "The surname is Guo."

units.zh: 暉曰：「吾當破國！」
units.en: Fuhui said: "I shall ruin the state!"
units.literal: Fuhui said: "I shall break the state!"

units.zh: 遂盡殺之。
units.en: and killed them to the last.
units.literal: and killed them all.

units.zh: 又至一家，問其姓，曰：「姓萬。」
units.en: At another house he asked; they said: "Wan."
units.literal: At another household he asked the surname; they said: "The surname is Wan."

units.zh: 暉曰：「吾殺萬家足矣。」
units.en: Fuhui said: "Slaying ten thousand houses is enough."
units.literal: Fuhui said: "Killing ten thousand households is enough for me."

units.zh: 又盡殺之。
units.en: and again killed them all.
units.literal: and again killed them all.

units.zh: 及明宗入魏，遂與在禮合謀，莊宗之禍自暉始。
units.en: When Mingzong entered Wei, Fuhui plotted on with Zaili, and Zhuangzong’s ruin began with Fuhui.
units.literal: When Mingzong entered Wei, Fuhui joined Zaili in further plots, and Zhuangzong’s disaster began with Fuhui.

units.zh: 明宗即位，暉自軍卒擢拜陳州刺史，終唐世常為刺史。
units.en: Mingzong raised him from the ranks to prefect of Chen, and through Tang he often held a prefecture.
units.literal: When Mingzong took the throne, Fuhui was raised from a soldier to prefect of Chen and through the Tang age was often a prefect.

units.zh: 晉天福中，以衛將軍居京師。
units.en: Under Jin Tianfu he was a guard general in the capital.
units.literal: In Jin’s Tianfu era he was a guard general living in the capital.

units.zh: 在禮已秉旄節，罷鎮來朝，暉往候之曰：「與公俱起甘陵，卒成大事，然由我發也，公今富貴，能恤我乎？
units.en: Zaili already held a commission and came to court on leave. Fuhui visited him: "We rose at Ganling and finished the great work, but I lit the fuse. You are rich now—will you spare me?
units.literal: Zaili already held a military commission; when he left his post and came to court, Fuhui called on him and said: "You and I rose together at Ganling and at last achieved the great affair—but it began with me. You are rich and honored now; can you spare a thought for me?

units.zh: 不然，禍起坐中！」
units.en: If not, ruin will rise from this seat!"
units.literal: If not, disaster will rise from this very seat!"

units.zh: 在禮懼，遽出器幣數千與之，而飲以酒，暉飲自若，不謝而去。
units.en: Zaili feared him, brought out thousands in goods at once, and poured wine. Fuhui drank easy and left without thanks.
units.literal: Zaili was afraid and at once brought out several thousand in vessels and goods and gave them to him, then poured wine. Fuhui drank at ease and left without thanks.

units.zh: 久之，為密州刺史。
units.en: Long after he was made prefect of Mi.
units.literal: After a long while he was made prefect of Mi.

units.zh: 契丹犯闕，暉率其州人奔於江南，李景以為歙州刺史、奉化軍節度使，鎮江州。
units.en: When the Khitan took the capital, Fuhui fled south with his prefecture. Li Jing made him prefect of She and commissioner of Fenghua at Jiang.
units.literal: When the Khitan stormed the capital, Fuhui led his prefecture’s people south to the Yangtze. Li Jing made him prefect of She, military commissioner of the Fenghua army, and stationed him at Jiang prefecture.

units.zh: 周師征淮，景以暉為北面行營應援使，屯清流關，為周師所敗，並其都監姚鳳皆被擒。
units.en: Zhou marched on the Huai. Jing named Fuhui northern relief commissioner and posted him at Qingliu Pass. Zhou broke him and took him with his overseer Yao Feng.
units.literal: When Zhou troops campaigned on the Huai, Jing made Fuhui northern relief commissioner of the field camp and stationed him at Qingliu Pass. Zhou troops defeated him and captured him together with his overseer Yao Feng.

units.zh: 世宗召見，暉金瘡被體，哀之，賜以金帶、鞍馬，後數日卒。
units.en: Shizong called him in. Golden wounds covered him; Shizong pitied him, gave belt and horse, and he died days later.
units.literal: Shizong summoned him to audience. Fuhui’s body was covered with golden wounds; Shizong pitied him, bestowed a gold belt and saddle horse, and several days later he died.

units.zh: 拜鳳左屯衛上將軍。
units.en: Feng was made Senior General of the Left Stationed Guard.
units.literal: Feng was made Senior General of the Left Stationed Guard.

units.zh: 唐景思
units.en: Tang Jingsi
units.literal: Tang Jingsi

units.zh: 唐景思，秦州人也。
units.en: Tang Jingsi came from Qin.
units.literal: Tang Jingsi was a native of Qinzhou.

units.zh: 幼善角觝，以屠狗為生。
units.en: As a boy he wrestled well and butchered dogs for a living.
units.literal: In youth he was skilled at wrestling and made his living butchering dogs.

units.zh: 後去為軍卒，累遷指揮使。
units.en: Later he became a soldier and rose to commander.
units.literal: Later he left home to become a soldier and was repeatedly promoted to commander.

units.zh: 唐魏王繼岌伐蜀，景思為蜀守固鎮。
units.en: When Jiji attacked Shu, Jingsi held Guzhen for Shu.
units.literal: When Tang’s Prince of Wei Jiji attacked Shu, Jingsi was Shu defender of Guzhen.

units.zh: 繼岌兵至，景思以城降，拜興州刺史。
units.en: Jiji arrived; Jingsi yielded the city and was made prefect of Xing.
units.literal: When Jiji’s army arrived, Jingsi surrendered the city and was made prefect of Xing.

units.zh: 晉高祖時，為貝州行軍司馬。
units.en: Under Jin Gaozu he was Bei’s marching marshal.
units.literal: Under Jin Gaozu he was marching marshal of Bei prefecture.

units.zh: 出帝時，契丹攻陷貝州，景思為趙延壽所得，以為壕砦使。
units.en: Under the Deposed Emperor the Khitan took Bei; Jingsi fell to Zhao Yanshou and was made trench commissioner.
units.literal: Under the Deposed Emperor the Khitan attacked and took Bei prefecture; Jingsi was taken by Zhao Yanshou and made trench-works commissioner.

units.zh: 契丹滅晉，拜景思亳州防禦使。
units.en: When the Khitan ended Jin, he was made defender of Bo.
units.literal: When the Khitan destroyed Jin, Jingsi was made defender of Bozhou.

units.zh: 漢高祖時，為鄧州行軍司馬，後為沿淮巡檢。
units.en: Under Han Gaozu he was Deng’s marching marshal, then Huai river inspector.
units.literal: Under Han Gaozu he was marching marshal of Deng and later inspector along the Huai.

units.zh: 漢法酷，而史弘肇用事，喜以告訐殺人。
units.en: Han law ran harsh. Shi Hongzhao held power and loved to kill on accusation.
units.literal: Han law was harsh, and Shi Hongzhao held power, delighting in killing men on denunciation.

units.zh: 景思有奴，嘗有所求不如意，即馳見弘肇，言景思與李景交通，而私畜兵甲。
units.en: Jingsi had a slave whose wish went unmet; the man galloped to Hongzhao and said Jingsi trafficked with Li Jing and hid arms.
units.literal: Jingsi had a slave who, when a request went unmet, at once galloped to see Hongzhao and said Jingsi was in contact with Li Jing and privately stored arms and armor.

units.zh: 弘肇遣吏將三十騎往收景思，奴謂吏曰：「景思勇者也，得則殺之，不然將失之也。」
units.en: Hongzhao sent thirty horse to seize him. The slave told them: "Jingsi is bold—take him and kill at once or you will lose him."
units.literal: Hongzhao sent officers with thirty horsemen to seize Jingsi. The slave told the officers: "Jingsi is a brave man—if you take him, kill him at once, or you will lose him."

units.zh: 吏至，景思迎前，以兩手抱吏呼冤，請詣獄自理。
units.en: They came; Jingsi met them, seized the officer in both arms, cried injustice, and asked prison to clear his name.
units.literal: When the officers arrived, Jingsi came forward, embraced the officer with both arms, cried injustice, and asked to go to prison to clear himself.

units.zh: 吏引奴與景思驗，景思曰：「我家在此，請索之。
units.en: They brought the slave to face him. Jingsi said: "My house is here—search it.
units.literal: The officers brought the slave to confront Jingsi. Jingsi said: "My household is here—search it.

units.zh: 有錢十千，為受外賂。
units.en: Ten thousand cash—that is outside bribe.
units.literal: There are ten thousand cash—proof I took outside bribes.

units.zh: 有甲一屬，為私畜兵。」
units.en: One suit of mail—that is private arms."
units.literal: There is one suit of armor—proof I privately stored troops."

units.zh: 吏索之，惟一衣笥，軍籍、糧簿而已。
units.en: They searched and found only one clothes chest, muster rolls, and grain books.
units.literal: The officers searched and found only one clothes basket, military registers, and grain ledgers.

units.zh: 吏閔而寬之，景思請械送京師以自明。
units.en: The officers pitied him and eased off. Jingsi asked fetters and the capital to clear himself.
units.literal: The officers pitied him and relented. Jingsi asked to be sent in fetters to the capital to clear himself.

units.zh: 景思有仆王知權在京師，聞景思被告，乃見弘肇，願先下獄明景思不反，弘肇憐之，送知權獄中，日勞以酒食。
units.en: Servant Wang Zhiquan was in the capital; hearing the charge, he saw Hongzhao and offered prison first to prove no revolt. Hongzhao pitied him and jailed Zhiquan, daily feeding him wine and meat.
units.literal: Jingsi had a servant Wang Zhiquan in the capital who, hearing Jingsi was accused, went to see Hongzhao and wished to enter prison first to prove Jingsi did not rebel. Hongzhao pitied him and sent Zhiquan into prison, daily treating him with wine and food.

units.zh: 景思既械就道，潁、亳之人隨至京師共明之。
units.en: Jingsi went fettered; men of Ying and Bo followed to the capital to clear him.
units.literal: Once Jingsi was fettered on the road, people of Ying and Bo followed him to the capital together to clear him.

units.zh: 弘肇乃鞫其奴，具伏，即奏斬奴而釋景思。
units.en: Hongzhao examined the slave; he confessed all. Hongzhao memorialized, beheaded the slave, and freed Jingsi.
units.literal: Hongzhao then interrogated the slave; he confessed fully. Hongzhao at once memorialized to behead the slave and release Jingsi.

units.zh: 後從世宗戰高平，世宗以所得漢降兵數千為效順指揮，以景思為指揮使，復戍淮上。
units.en: Later he followed Shizong at Gaoping. Shizong formed several thousand Han surrender troops into the Obedient Command, made Jingsi commander, and posted him again on the Huai.
units.literal: Later he followed Shizong at the battle of Gaoping. Shizong made several thousand Han surrender troops into the Obedient Command and made Jingsi its commander, again garrisoning him on the Huai.

units.zh: 周師伐淮南，以功領饒州刺史，遷濠州刺史，兵攻濠州，以戰傷重卒，贈武清軍節度使。
units.en: When Zhou armies marched on Huainan, merit made him Rao prefect, then Hao prefect. Enemy troops struck Hao; he died of his wounds and was posthumously made military commissioner of Wuqing.
units.literal: When Zhou armies campaigned against Huainan, for merit he was made prefect of Rao, then transferred to Hao prefecture; troops attacked Hao prefecture, and he died of severe battle wounds; he was posthumously made military commissioner of Wuqing.

units.zh: 王進
units.en: Wang Jin
units.literal: Wang Jin

units.zh: 王進，幽州良鄉人也。
units.en: Wang Jin came from Liangxiang in Youzhou.
units.literal: Wang Jin was a native of Liangxiang in Youzhou.

units.zh: 為人勇悍，走及奔馬。
units.en: He was fierce and bold, and could outrun a galloping horse.
units.literal: As a man he was fierce and bold, and in running he could keep pace with galloping horses.

units.zh: 少聚徒為盜，鄉里患之，符彥超遣人以賂招置麾下。
units.en: In youth he gathered a band and robbed the countryside. Fu Yanchao bribed him into service.
units.literal: In youth he gathered followers and became a bandit; the neighborhood suffered from him. Fu Yanchao sent men with bribes to recruit him and placed him under his command.

units.zh: 彥超鎮安遠軍，軍中有變，遣進馳奏京師，明宗怪其來速，嘉其足力，以隸寧衞指揮。
units.en: Yanchao held Anyuan army when the camp mutinied. He sent Jin racing to the capital. Mingzong marveled at his speed and praised his legs, then assigned him to the Ningwei Guard.
units.literal: When Yanchao governed Anyuan army, there was a mutiny in the camp. He sent Jin racing to report to the capital. Mingzong marveled at his swift arrival and praised his fleet feet, then assigned him to the Ningwei Guard.

units.zh: 漢高祖為侍衞親軍指揮使，以進為軍校。
units.en: When Han Gaozu commanded the Palace Guard, he made Jin a company officer.
units.literal: When Han Gaozu was commander of the Palace Guard, he made Jin a company officer.

units.zh: 高祖鎮河東，因以之從，每有急，遣進馳至京師，往返不過五六日，由是愈親愛之，累遷奉國軍都指揮使。
units.en: When Gaozu governed Hedong, Jin went with him. In every crisis Gaozu sent him racing to the capital—a round trip of five or six days at most. Gaozu grew ever fonder and raised him to commander of the Fengguo army.
units.literal: When Gaozu governed Hedong, Jin followed him. Whenever there was urgency, Gaozu sent Jin racing to the capital; the round trip took no more than five or six days. From this he grew ever closer to Jin and repeatedly promoted him, until he became commander of the Fengguo army.

units.zh: 從周太祖起魏，遷虎捷右廂都指揮使。
units.en: He followed Zhou Taizu in the Wei rising and became commander of the right wing of the Tiger Swift Army.
units.literal: He followed Zhou Taizu in rising at Wei and was transferred to commander of the right wing of the Tiger Swift Army.

units.zh: 歷汝、鄭二州防禦使、彰德軍節度使。
units.en: He was defender of Ru and Zheng in turn and military commissioner of Zhangde.
units.literal: He successively served as defender of Ru and Zheng prefectures and military commissioner of the Zhangde army.

units.zh: 顯德元年秋，一本作初。
units.en: In autumn of the first year of Xiande—one edition reads chu instead of qiu.
units.literal: In autumn of the first year of Xiande—one edition reads chu instead of qiu.

units.zh: 以疾卒，贈太師。
units.en: He died of illness and was posthumously made Grand Preceptor.
units.literal: He died of illness and was posthumously made Grand Preceptor.

units.zh: 嗚呼！
units.en: Alas!
units.literal: Alas!

units.zh: 予述舊史，至於王進之事，未嘗不廢書而嘆曰：甚哉，五代之君，皆武人崛起，其所與俱勇夫悍卒，各裂土地封侯王，何異豺狼之牧斯人也！
units.en: When I set down the old histories and came to Wang Jin, I never failed to lay aside the book and sigh: How extreme! Every ruler of the Five Dynasties was a warrior risen from the ranks; the bold and brutal men who rose with him carved out domains and were made marquises and kings—what but wolves herding sheep?
units.literal: When I set down the old histories and came to Wang Jin’s story, I never failed to lay aside the book and sigh: How extreme! The rulers of the Five Dynasties all rose as men of war; the fierce soldiers and brutal troops who rose with them each carved out land and were enfeoffed as marquises and kings—what difference is there from wolves herding these people!

units.zh: 雖其附托遭遇，出於一時之幸，然猶必皆橫身陣敵，非有百夫之勇，則必一日之勞。
units.en: Even when favor and fortune came from a moment’s luck, they still had to throw themselves into the line—without the strength of a hundred men, at least a day’s worth of fighting.
units.literal: Though their patronage and fortune came from a moment’s luck, they still had to throw themselves into battle—without the courage of a hundred men, at least a day’s labor in the ranks.

units.zh: 至如進者，徒以疾足善走而秉旄節，何其甚歟！
units.en: Jin held a commissioner’s baton for nothing but swift feet and a gift for running—how extreme is that!
units.literal: As for Jin, he held a commissioner’s baton merely for swift feet and a gift for running—how extreme is that!

units.zh: 豈非名器之用，隨世而輕重者歟？
units.en: Is it not that rank and title grow light or heavy with the times?
units.literal: Is it not that the weight of rank and title shifts with the age?

units.zh: 世治則君子居之而重，世亂則小人易得而輕歟？
units.en: In ordered times gentlemen hold them and they weigh heavy; in chaotic times petty men seize them easily and they weigh light?
units.literal: When the age is well ordered, gentlemen hold them and they weigh heavy; when the age is chaotic, petty men obtain them easily and they weigh light?

units.zh: 抑因緣僥幸，未始不有，而尤多於亂世，既其極也，遂至於是歟？
units.en: Or is it that luck has never been absent, but runs riot in chaotic ages—and at the extreme, things come to this?
units.literal: Or is it that chance and luck have never been absent, but abound above all in chaotic ages—and at the extreme, things come to this?

units.zh: 豈其又有甚於是者歟？
units.en: And are there yet cases worse than this?
units.literal: And are there yet cases worse than this?

units.zh: 當此之時，為國長者不過十餘年，短者三四年至一二年。
units.en: In that age the longest reign was barely a dozen years; the shortest ran three or four, or one or two.
units.literal: In that age, a man who held the state did so for no more than a dozen years—at shortest three or four years, or one or two.

units.zh: 天下之人，視其上易君代國，如更戍長無異，蓋其輕如此，況其下者乎！
units.en: Men under heaven watched their betters change rulers and dynasties as casually as a garrison chief is rotated—so lightly were they held; how much more those below!
units.literal: Men under heaven watched their superiors change rulers and dynasties as casually as a garrison chief is replaced—so lightly were they held; how much more those below!

units.zh: 如進等者，豈足道哉！
units.en: Men like Jin—what is there to speak of!
units.literal: Men like Jin—what is there to speak of!

units.zh: 《易》否泰消長，君子小人常相上下，視在上者如進等，則其在下者可知矣。
units.en: The Changes tells how pi and tai wax and wane and gentleman and petty man trade places. When those on high are like Jin, those below may be guessed.
units.literal: In the Changes, pi and tai wax and wane; gentleman and petty man constantly trade places above and below. When those on high are like Jin, those below may be known.

units.zh: 予書進事，所以哀斯人之亂，而見當時賢人君子之在下者，可勝道哉！
units.en: I record Jin’s story to mourn that chaos—and to show how many worthy men were kept below. What sighs could number them all!
units.literal: I record Jin’s story to mourn the chaos of that age—and to show how many worthy gentlemen and scholars of the time were kept below. What sighs could number them all!

units.zh: 可勝道哉！
units.en: What sighs could number them all!
units.literal: What sighs could number them all!

units.zh: 常思
units.en: Chang Si
units.literal: Chang Si

units.zh: 常思字克恭，太原人也。
units.en: Chang Si, styled Kegong, came from Taiyuan.
units.literal: Chang Si, courtesy name Kegong, was a native of Taiyuan.

units.zh: 初從唐莊宗為卒，後為長劍指揮使。
units.en: He first followed Zhuangzong as a soldier and later commanded the Long Sword.
units.literal: At first he followed Tang’s Zhuangzong as a soldier and later became commander of the Long Sword.

units.zh: 歷唐、晉為六軍都虞候。
units.en: Under Tang and Jin he was deputy commander of the Six Armies.
units.literal: Under Tang and Jin he served as deputy commander of the Six Armies.

units.zh: 漢高祖為河東節度使，以思為牢城指揮使。
units.en: When Han Gaozu governed Hedong, he made Si commander of the Laocheng garrison.
units.literal: When Han Gaozu was military governor of Hedong, he made Si commander of the Laocheng garrison.

units.zh: 高祖入立，領武勝軍節度使，徙鎮昭義。
units.en: When Gaozu took the throne, Si held the Wusheng commission and was shifted to Zhaoyi.
units.literal: When Gaozu entered and took the throne, Si held the Wusheng army commission and was transferred to govern Zhaoyi.

units.zh: 思起軍卒，未嘗有戰功，徒以幸會漢興，遂秉旄節。
units.en: Si rose from the ranks without battle merit and held a commissioner’s baton only by the luck of Han’s rise.
units.literal: Si rose from a soldier and had never won battle merit; he held a commissioner’s baton only by the luck of Han’s rise.

units.zh: 在潞州五年，以聚斂為事，而性鄙儉。
units.en: Five years at Luzhou he spent extorting wealth, yet by nature he was stingy and frugal.
units.literal: For five years at Luzhou he made extortion his business, yet by nature he was mean and frugal.

units.zh: 初，思微時，周太祖方少孤無依，食于思家，以思為叔，後思與周太祖俱遭漢以取富貴。
units.en: When Si was still obscure, young Zhou Taizu was orphaned and ate at his home, calling him uncle. Later both rode Han’s rise to wealth and rank.
units.literal: At first, when Si was still obscure, Zhou Taizu was young, orphaned, and without support, and ate at Si’s home, calling Si uncle. Later both Si and Zhou Taizu rode Han’s rise to wealth and rank.

units.zh: 周太祖已即位，每呼思為常叔，拜其妻，如家人禮。
units.en: Once Zhou Taizu reigned, he always called Si Uncle Chang and bowed to his wife as kin.
units.literal: After Zhou Taizu had taken the throne, he always called Si Uncle Chang and bowed to his wife with the courtesy of family.

units.zh: 廣順三年，徙鎮歸德，居三年來朝，又徙平盧，思因啟曰：「臣居宋，宋民負臣絲息十萬兩，願以券上進。」
units.en: In the third year of Guangshun he was moved to Guide. Three years later he came to court, then was shifted to Pinglu. Si petitioned: "When I governed Song, the people owed me one hundred thousand taels in silk interest. I wish to present the bonds to Your Majesty."
units.literal: In the third year of Guangshun he was transferred to govern Guide. After three years in post he came to court, then was moved again to Pinglu. Si thereupon petitioned, saying: "When I governed Song, the people of Song owed me one hundred thousand taels in silk interest. I wish to present the bonds to Your Majesty."

units.zh: 太祖頷之，即焚其券，詔宋州悉蠲除之。
units.en: Taizu nodded, burned the bonds, and ordered Song prefecture to forgive the debts entirely.
units.literal: Taizu nodded assent, then burned the bonds and ordered Song prefecture to forgive the debts entirely.

units.zh: 思居青州，踰年得疾，歸于洛陽，卒，贈中書令。
units.en: At Qingzhou he fell ill within a year, returned to Luoyang, and died. He was posthumously made Grand Councilor.
units.literal: Si governed Qingzhou; after more than a year he fell ill, returned to Luoyang, and died. He was posthumously made Grand Councilor.

units.zh: 孫方諫
units.en: Sun Fangjian
units.literal: Sun Fangjian

units.zh: 孫方諫，鄭州清苑人也。
units.en: Sun Fangjian came from Qingyuan in Zheng prefecture.
units.literal: Sun Fangjian was a man of Qingyuan in Zheng prefecture.

units.zh: 初，定州西北有狼山堡，定人常保以避契丹，有尼深意居其中，以佛法誘民，民多歸之。
units.en: Northwest of Ding stood Langshan Fort, where Ding people sheltered from the Khitan. A nun, Shenyi, lived there and drew folk by Buddhist teaching; many followed her.
units.literal: At first, northwest of Ding prefecture there was Langshan Fort; the people of Ding often sheltered there to escape the Khitan. A nun named Shenyi lived within it and drew the people by Buddhist teaching; many followed her.

units.zh: 後尼死，堡人言其屍不朽，因奉而事之。
units.en: When she died, the fort folk said her body did not decay and they honored and served her.
units.literal: When the nun died, the fort people said her corpse did not decay, and they honored and served her.

units.zh: 尼姓孫氏，方諫自以為尼族人，即繼行其法，堡人推以為主。
units.en: The nun was surnamed Sun; Fangjian claimed her clan, carried on her practices, and the fort folk made him their leader.
units.literal: The nun’s surname was Sun; Fangjian took himself for kin of the nun’s clan, then carried on her practices, and the fort people pushed him as their leader.

units.zh: 晉出帝時，義武軍節度使惡方諫聚徒山中，恐為邊患，因表以為遊奕使。
units.en: Under Jin’s Last Emperor the Yiwu commissioner hated Fangjian for gathering men in the hills and feared border trouble; he memorialized to make him roving patrol commissioner.
units.literal: In the Last Emperor’s time of Jin, the military commissioner of the Yiwu army hated Fangjian for gathering followers in the hills and feared a border trouble; he therefore memorialized to make him roving patrol commissioner.

units.zh: 方諫因有所求不得，乃北通契丹。
units.en: When a request went unanswered, Fangjian turned to the Khitan in the north.
units.literal: Fangjian, because a request went unanswered, then opened relations with the Khitan in the north.

units.zh: 契丹後滅晉，以方諫為義武軍節度使。
units.en: The Khitan later destroyed Jin and made Fangjian military commissioner of Yiwu.
units.literal: Afterward the Khitan destroyed Jin and made Fangjian military commissioner of the Yiwu army.

units.zh: 已而徙方諫於雲中，方諫不受命，率其徒復入狼山。
units.en: Soon they moved him to Yunzhong; he refused and led his band back into Langshan Fort.
units.literal: Soon they moved Fangjian to Yunzhong; Fangjian would not accept the order and led his followers back into Langshan Fort.

units.zh: 漢高祖起，契丹縱火燒定州，虜其人民北去。
units.en: Han Gaozu rose; the Khitan burned Ding prefecture and drove its people north as captives.
units.literal: Han Gaozu rose; the Khitan set fire to Ding prefecture and carried its people north as captives.

units.zh: 方諫聞之，自狼山入，據之以歸漢，高祖嘉之，即拜方諫義武軍節度使。
units.en: Fangjian marched out of Langshan, seized the city, and submitted to Han; Gaozu praised him and at once restored him as Yiwu commissioner.
units.literal: When Fangjian heard of it, he came out from Langshan, seized the place, and submitted to Han; Gaozu praised him and at once made him military commissioner of the Yiwu army.

units.zh: 周太祖時，徙鎮鎮國，以其弟行友為定州留後。
units.en: Under Zhou Taizu he was moved to Zhenguo; his younger brother Xingyou was left as acting governor of Ding.
units.literal: Under Zhou Taizu he was moved to Zhenguo, and his younger brother Xingyou was made acting governor of Ding.

units.zh: 世宗攻太原，方諫朝於行在，從還京，至洛得疾，徙鎮匡國，卒於洛陽，年六十二，贈太師。
units.en: When Shizong attacked Taiyuan, Fangjian came to the imperial camp, followed him home, fell ill at Luoyang, was moved to Kuangguo, and died there at sixty-two; he was posthumously made Grand Preceptor.
units.literal: When Shizong attacked Taiyuan, Fangjian came to court at the imperial camp, followed him back to the capital, fell ill at Luoyang, was moved to Kuangguo, and died at Luoyang at the age of sixty-two; he was posthumously made Grand Preceptor.

units.zh: 晉王遣都將李嗣昭、李存審、王建及率師來援同州，戰於城下。
units.en: The Prince of Jin sent Li Sizhao, Li Cunshen, and Wang Jianji to relieve Tongzhou and battle was joined under the walls.
units.literal: The Prince of Jin sent commanders Li Sizhao, Li Cunshen, and Wang Jianji with troops to relieve Tongzhou; they fought below the walls.

units.zh: 夏四月己巳，晉王即唐帝位於魏州，改天祐二十年為同光元年。
units.en: On jisi in the fourth month of summer the Prince of Jin took the Tang throne at Weizhou, renaming Tianyou 20 Tongguang 1.
units.literal: On jisi in the fourth month of summer the Prince of Jin assumed the Tang throne at Weizhou, changing Tianyou 20 to Tongguang 1.

units.zh: 時晉王方攻鎮州，故思遠乘虛以襲之，陷成安，而思遠遂急攻德勝北城，晉將李存審極力拒守。
units.en: While the Prince of Jin besieged Zhenzhou, Siyuan took Cheng'an and stormed Desheng’s north wall; Li Cunshen held firm.
units.literal: At the time the Prince of Jin was attacking Zhenzhou; hence Siyuan seized the opening to strike, took Cheng'an, and then urgently attacked Desheng’s northern city; Jin commander Li Cunshen resisted with utmost strength.

units.zh: 二月，晉王以兵至，思遠收軍而退，復保楊村。
units.en: In the second month the Prince of Jin came up; Siyuan withdrew to Yang village.
units.literal: In the second month the Prince of Jin arrived with troops; Siyuan gathered the army and withdrew, again holding Yang village.

units.zh: 唐帝棄德勝之北城，並軍保楊劉。
units.en: The Tang emperor abandoned Desheng’s north wall and concentrated at Yangliu.
units.literal: The Tang Emperor abandoned Desheng’s northern city and combined the army to hold Yangliu.

units.zh: 六月乙亥，唐帝引軍援楊劉，潛軍至博州，築壘於河東岸。
units.en: On yihai in the sixth month the Tang emperor relieved Yangliu while secretly fortifying east of Bozhou.
units.literal: On yihai in the sixth month the Tang Emperor led troops to relieve Yangliu, secretly moving the army to Bozhou and building ramparts on the river’s east bank.

units.zh: 秋七月丁未，唐帝引軍沿河而南。
units.en: On dingwei in the seventh month the Tang emperor led his army south along the river.
units.literal: On dingwei in the seventh month of autumn the Tang Emperor led troops south along the river.

units.zh: 庚寅，唐帝軍於胡城，先鋒將康延孝率百騎奔於唐，盡泄其軍機。
units.en: On gengyin at Hucheng vanguard Kang Yanxiao defected with a hundred riders and betrayed Liang dispositions.
units.literal: On gengyin the Tang Emperor’s army was at Hucheng; vanguard commander Kang Yanxiao led a hundred horsemen to defect to Tang and fully revealed our military plans.

units.zh: 甲戌，唐帝引師襲中都，王彥章兵潰，於是彥章與監軍張漢傑及趙廷隱、劉嗣彬、李知節、唐文通、王山興等皆為唐人所獲。
units.en: On jiaxu the Tang emperor stormed Zhongdu; Yanzhang’s army broke; he, Zhang Hanjie, Zhao Tingyin, and others were taken.
units.literal: On jiaxu the Tang Emperor led troops to strike Zhongdu; Wang Yanzhang’s army collapsed; thereupon Yanzhang, army supervisor Zhang Hanjie, Zhao Tingyin, Liu Sibin, Li Zhijie, Tang Wentong, Wang Shanxing, and others were all captured by Tang men.

units.zh: 帝置傳國寶於臥內，俄失其所在，已為左右所竊迎唐帝矣。
units.en: He laid the seal in his chamber; it vanished—courtiers had stolen it to greet the Tang emperor.
units.literal: The Emperor placed the dynastic seal in the sleeping chamber; soon it lost its place—it had already been stolen by attendants to welcome the Tang Emperor.

units.zh: 唐帝入宮，妃郭氏號泣迎拜。
units.en: The Tang emperor entered the palace; Consort Guo wept and bowed in welcome.
units.literal: The Tang Emperor entered the palace; consort Guo wailed and came forward to bow.

units.zh: 唐帝初入東京，聞帝殂，憮然歎曰：「敵惠敵怨，不在後嗣。
units.en: Entering the Eastern Capital, the Tang emperor learned of the Last Emperor’s death and sighed: "Grudges need not pass to sons.
units.literal: When the Tang Emperor first entered the Eastern Capital and heard the Emperor had died, he sighed in dejection: "Enemy kindness and enemy hatred do not lie in later generations.

units.zh: 九月庚寅，以供奉官郎公遠充契丹歡好使。
units.en: On gengyin in the ninth month Palace Attendant Lang Gongyuan was sent as envoy of goodwill to the Khitan.
units.literal: On gengyin in the ninth month, Palace Attendant Lang Gongyuan was made Khitan Goodwill envoy.

units.zh: 龍德二年春正月，戴思遠率師襲魏州。
units.en: In the first month of Longde 2 Dai Siyuan raided Weizhou.
units.literal: In the first month of spring of Longde 2, Dai Siyuan led troops to raid Weizhou.

units.zh: 尋詔河南尹張全義收葬之，其首藏於太社。
units.en: He ordered Zhang Quanyi to bury the body; the head was kept at the Grand Altar.
units.literal: Soon an edict ordered Henan Intendant Zhang Quanyi to collect and bury him; his head was stored at the Grand Altar.

units.zh: 先是，繼韜父嗣昭為潞州節度使，戰歿於鎮州城下，晉王欲以嗣昭長子繼儔襲父位。
units.en: His father Li Sizhao had held Luzhou and died at Zhenzhou; the Prince of Jin meant to give the post to eldest son Jichou.
units.literal: Earlier, Jiyao’s father Sizhao was Luzhou military commissioner and fell in battle below Zhenzhou city; the Prince of Jin wished to let Sizhao’s eldest son Jichou succeed his father’s post.

units.zh: 朕與梁主十年對壘，恨不生見其面。」
units.en: We fought ten years; I regret never meeting him alive."
units.literal: I and the Liang ruler faced each other in battle ten years, regretting I did not see his face in life."

units.zh: 裨將趙在禮聞軍亂，衣不及帶，將逾垣而遁，亂兵追及，白刃環之曰：「公能為帥否？
units.en: Lieutenant Zhao Zaili, hearing the army was in chaos, had no time to belt his robe and was about to climb over the wall to flee when the mutineers caught him; blades ringed him and they said, "Can you be commander?
units.literal: Lieutenant Zhao Zaili, hearing the army in chaos, had not time to belt his robe and was about to climb the wall to flee when the mutineers overtook him; blades ringed him and they said, "Can you be commander?

units.zh: 在禮懼，即曰：「吾能為之。」
units.en: Terrified, Zhao Zaili immediately said, "I can do it."
units.literal: Terrified, Zhao Zaili immediately said, "I can do it."

units.zh: 詰旦，擁在禮趨臨清，剽永濟、館陶。
units.en: At dawn they marched Zhao Zaili toward Linqing and raided Yongji and Guantao.
units.literal: At dawn they drove Zaili toward Linqing and plundered Yongji and Guantao.

units.zh: 晡晚，趙在禮引諸軍據宮城，署皇甫暉等為都虞候、斬斫使，諸軍大掠。
units.en: By evening Zhao Zaili held the palace, made Huangfu Hui adjutant, and the army looted Ye.
units.literal: In late afternoon Zhao Zaili led the armies to seize the palace city, appointing Huangfu Hui and others overall adjutants and execution officers; the armies plundered greatly.

units.zh: 興唐尹王正言謁在禮，望塵再拜。
units.en: Wang Zhengyan bowed twice in the dust to Zhao Zaili.
units.literal: Xingtang prefect Wang Zhengyan called on Zaili and twice bowed in the dust.

units.zh: 是日，眾推在禮為兵馬留後，草奏以聞。
units.en: That day the mutineers made Zhao Zaili acting commissioner and memorialized court.
units.literal: That day the crowd pushed Zaili as acting military commissioner and drafted a memorial to report it.

units.zh: 辛丑，元行欽至鄴都，進攻南門，以詔書招諭城中，趙在禮獻羊酒勞軍，登城遙拜行欽曰：「將士經年離隔父母，不取敕旨歸寧，上貽聖憂，追悔何及！
units.en: On xinchou Yuan Xingqin reached Ye, attacked the south gate, and used an edict to summon the city; Zhao Zaili presented sheep and wine to comfort the army and bowed from the wall to Xingqin, saying, "The soldiers have been separated from their parents for years; by returning home without edict, they have burdened the sage with worry. What regret can suffice!
units.literal: On xinchou Yuan Xingqin reached Ye, attacked the south gate, and with an edict summoned the city; Zhao Zaili presented sheep and wine to comfort the army and from the wall bowed distantly to Xingqin, saying, "The troops were separated from parents for years and, not taking the edict to return home, burdened the sage—what regret can suffice!

units.zh: 眾遂呼噪，中夜燔劫貝郡。
units.en: The mutineers shouted and looted Beizhou at midnight.
units.literal: The crowd then shouted and at midnight burned and plundered Beizhou.

units.zh: 否則頭隨刃落！」
units.en: If not, your head will fall with the blade!"
units.literal: If not, your head follows the blade!"

units.zh: 儻公善為敷奏，俾從渙汗，某等亦不敢不改過自新。」
units.en: If you, sir, will memorialize well and let us follow the edict of grace, we too dare not fail to reform ourselves."
units.literal: If you, sir, will memorialize well and let us follow the edict of grace, we too dare not fail to reform."

units.zh: 以天雄軍節度使石敬瑭為御營使。
units.en: Shi Jingtang of Tianxiong became imperial camp commissioner.
units.literal: Tianxiong army military commissioner Shi Jingtang was made imperial camp commissioner.

units.zh: 以易州刺史孫行友為定州留後。
units.en: Sun Xingyou, Prefect of Yi, was appointed Acting Commissioner of Ding.
units.literal: Sun Xingyou, Prefect of Yi prefecture, was made Acting Commissioner of Ding prefecture.

units.zh: 乙酉，前蔡州刺史董璋權知宣義軍軍州事。
units.en: On yiyou, Dong Zhang, former prefect of Cai, was given acting charge of Xuanyi Army affairs.
units.literal: On yiyou, former Cai prefect Dong Zhang was made acting Xuanyi Army military and prefectural commissioner.

units.zh: 二月甲申，晉王攻我黎陽，劉鄩拒之而退。
units.en: On jiashen in the second month, the Prince of Jin attacked Liyang; Liu Xun held him off and forced a withdrawal.
units.literal: On jiashen in the second month, the Prince of Jin attacked our Liyang; Liu Xun resisted him and drove him back.

units.zh: 貞明三年春正月戊午，以前淄州刺史高允奇為右羽林統軍。
units.en: On wuwu in the first month of Zhenming 3, Gao Yunqi, former Inspector of Zi Prefecture, was appointed commander of the Right Feathered Forest.
units.literal: On wuwu, in the first month of spring of Zhenming 3, former Zi Prefecture Inspector Gao Yunqi was made commander of the Right Feathered Forest.

units.zh: 軍士皇甫暉等因夜聚蒱博不勝，遂作亂，劫都將楊仁晸曰：「我輩十有餘年為國家效命，甲不離體，已至吞並天下，主上未垂恩澤，翻有猜嫌。
units.en: Soldiers Huangfu Hui and others, after losing at night gambling, mutinied and seized commander Yang Renjian, saying, "For more than ten years we have served the state, never taking armor from our bodies, until the realm was conquered; yet the sovereign has shown us no grace and instead suspects us.
units.literal: Soldiers Huangfu Hui and others, having lost at night gambling, then made rebellion and seized commander Yang Renjian, saying, "We have served the state more than ten years, armor never off our bodies, until the realm was swallowed up—yet the sovereign has not bestowed grace and instead harbors suspicion.

units.zh: 皇甫暉聚眾大詬，即壞詔。
units.en: Huangfu Hui cursed and tore up the edict.
units.literal: Huangfu Hui gathered the crowd and cursed loudly, then destroyed the edict.

units.zh: 防戍邊遠，經年離阻鄉國，及得代歸，去家咫尺，不令與家屬相見。
units.en: After years on distant frontiers, cut off from home, when they were finally relieved and came within a stone's throw of home, they were still denied even a glimpse of their families.
units.literal: Guarding distant frontiers, separated from home for years, and on relief returning home was within a foot—yet we were not allowed to see kin.

units.zh: 今聞皇后弑逆，京邑已亂，將士各欲歸府寧親，請公同行。」
units.en: Now we hear the Empress has committed regicide and the capital is in chaos; the soldiers all wish to return home to see their families. Please, sir, go with us."
units.literal: Now we hear the Empress committed regicide and the capital is in chaos; the troops each wish to return home—please, sir, go with us."

units.zh: 壬戌，幽州節度使趙德鈞兼北面行營招討使，鎮州節度使範延光加檢校太傅。
units.en: On renxu Zhao Dejun of Youzhou became northern campaign commissioner and Fan Yanguang of Zhen inspector grand mentor.
units.literal: On renxu, Youzhou military commissioner Zhao Dejun was given added northern campaign headquarters commissioner; Zhen prefecture military commissioner Fan Yanguang was given Inspector Grand Mentor by inspection.

units.zh: 先是，李景遣其弟偽齊王達率全軍來援壽州，達留駐濠州，遣其將許文縝、邊鎬、朱元領兵數萬，溯淮而上，至紫金山，設十餘寨，與城內烽火相應。
units.en: Earlier Li Jing had sent his brother, the puppet Prince of Qi Da, at the head of the full Southern Tang army to relieve Shouzhou. Da stayed at Haozhou and dispatched Xu Wenzhen, Bian Hao, and Zhu Yuan with tens of thousands of men up the Huai to Purple Gold Mountain, where they pitched more than ten camps linked by beacon fire to the besieged city.
units.literal: Earlier, Li Jing had sent his younger brother, the unrecognized Prince of Qi, Da, leading the full army to relieve Shouzhou; Da remained at Haozhou and sent his generals Xu Wenzhen, Bian Hao, and Zhu Yuan with tens of thousands of troops up the Huai to Purple Gold Mountain, establishing more than ten camps in beacon contact with the city.

units.zh: 許王從益，明宗之幼子也。
units.en: Prince Xu Congyi was Mingzong's youngest son.
units.literal: Prince Xu Congyi was Emperor Mingzong's youngest son.

units.zh: 晉高祖即位，以皇后即其姊也，乃養從益於宮中。
units.en: When Gaozu of Jin took the throne, the empress being his elder sister, Congyi was raised in the palace.
units.literal: When Gaozu of Jin took the throne, because the empress was his elder sister, Congyi was raised within the palace.

units.zh: 守陵開運末，契丹主至汴，以從益遙領曹州節度使，復封許王，與王妃尋歸西京。
units.en: While guarding the imperial tombs in late Kaiyun, the Khitan ruler reached Bian. Congyi was given titular command of Caozhou, again enfeoffed as Prince of Xu, and soon returned to the Western Capital with his consort.
units.literal: While guarding the tombs at the end of Kaiyun, the Khitan ruler came to Bian; Congyi was made titular military commissioner of Caozhou at a distance, again enfeoffed as Prince of Xu, and soon returned to the Western Capital with his princess consort.

units.zh: 漢高祖怒，車駕將至闕，從益與王妃俱賜死於私第，時年十七；
units.en: Gaozu of Han was enraged. As the imperial carriage neared the capital, Congyi and his consort were both ordered to die in their private residence. He was seventeen;
units.literal: Gaozu of Han was angry; as the imperial carriage was about to reach the palace, Congyi and his princess consort were both granted death in their private residence; he was seventeen years old;

units.zh: 從璨為權臣所忌，從益為強敵所脅，俱不得其死，亦良可傷哉！
units.en: Congcan was destroyed by a powerful minister, Congyi was coerced by a strong enemy—neither died a natural death. How lamentable!
units.literal: Congcan was resented by a powerful minister, Congyi was coerced by a strong enemy—neither met a natural death; this too is deeply lamentable!

units.zh: 長興末，封許王。
units.en: At the end of the Changxing era he was enfeoffed as Prince of Xu.
units.literal: At the end of Changxing he was enfeoffed as Prince of Xu.

units.zh: 〈（《五代史闕文》：漢高祖自太原起軍建號，至洛陽，會郭從義先入京師，受密旨殺王淑妃與許王從益。
units.en: (Lost Writings of the History of the Five Dynasties records that Gaozu of Han raised his army at Taiyuan and established his reign. Reaching Luoyang, he found Guo Congyi already in the capital with a secret order to kill Consort Wang Shufei and Prince Xu Congyi.
units.literal: (Lost Writings of the History of the Five Dynasties: Gaozu of Han raised an army at Taiyuan and established his reign; reaching Luoyang, he met Guo Congyi, who had entered the capital first and received a secret order to kill Consort Wang Shufei and Prince Xu Congyi.

units.zh: 晉天福中，以從益為二王後，改封郇國公，食邑三千戶。
units.en: During Jin Tianfu he was made heir to the second princely rank, retitled Duke of Xun, with a fief of three thousand households.
units.literal: During Tianfu of Jin, Congyi was made heir to the second prince rank, his title was changed to Duke of Xun, and his fief was three thousand households.

units.zh: 乃詐稱契丹主命，遣人迎從益於洛陽，令知南朝軍國事。
units.en: so he falsely claimed the Khitan ruler's command, sent men to summon Congyi from Luoyang, and installed him to govern the southern court's military and civil affairs.
units.literal: therefore he falsely claimed the Khitan ruler's command, sent men to welcome Congyi from Luoyang, and ordered him to manage the military and civil affairs of the southern court.

units.zh: 會契丹主死，其汴州節度使蕭翰謀歸北地，慮中原無主，軍民大亂，則己亦不得按轡徐歸矣；
units.en: When the Khitan ruler died, his Bianzhou military commissioner Xiao Han planned to return north. He feared that with no ruler in the Central Plains and army and people in chaos, he himself could not withdraw at leisure;
units.literal: When the Khitan ruler died, his Bianzhou military commissioner Xiao Han planned to return north and feared that with no ruler in central China and army and people in great disorder, he himself would be unable to rein in his horse and withdraw at leisure;

units.zh: 時人哀之。
units.en: and the people pitied him.
units.literal: people of the time pitied him.

units.zh: 從益於崇元殿見群官。
units.en: Congyi received the assembled officials in Chongyuan Hall.
units.literal: Congyi received the assembled officials in Chongyuan Hall.

units.zh: 先帝潛龍時，亦上疏請解其兵權，以備非常之變，少主不納，未幾先帝遂有天下。
units.en: When Taizu was still in obscurity, Tao also memorialized to strip him of military authority against extraordinary change; the young lord did not accept it, and before long Taizu possessed the realm.
units.literal: When the late emperor was still in obscurity, he too submitted a memorial asking that military authority be removed to guard against extraordinary change; the young lord did not accept it, and before long the late emperor came to possess the realm.

units.zh: 乃以皇子繼岌為亞獻，皇弟存紀為終獻。
units.en: Jiji was made second libationer and Cunji final libationer.
units.literal: Prince Jiji was then made second libationer and the Emperor's brother Cunji final libationer.

units.zh: 幸左龍武軍，以皇子繼岌代張全義判六軍諸衛事故也。
units.en: Cunxu visited the Left Dragon Martial Army as Prince Jiji took over Zhang Quanyi's charge of the Six Armies and Guards.
units.literal: The Emperor visited the Left Dragon Martial Army because the prince Jiji was replacing Zhang Quanyi in overseeing the Six Armies and Imperial Guards.

units.zh: 帝意欲歸之，會冀州刺史楊檀罷郡至闕，帝問其事，奏曰：「此輩來援王都，謀危社稷，陛下寬慈，貸其生命。
units.en: Mingzong favored return until Yang Tan of Jizhou said: "they had aided Wang Du against the state and mercy should not send them back.
units.literal: The Emperor wished to return them; it happened that Jizhou prefect Yang Tan left his prefecture and reached court; the Emperor asked about the matter; he memorialized: "These men came to aid Wang Du, plotting to endanger the state; Your Majesty's broad mercy spared their lives.

units.zh: 苟若歸之，必復向南放箭，既知中國事情，為患深矣。」
units.en: Returned, they would raid south again with dangerous knowledge of the realm."
units.literal: If returned, they will surely again shoot arrows south; knowing China's affairs, the harm would be deep."

units.zh: 是月，周主威殂，養子晉王柴榮嗣立。
units.en: That month Zhou's ruler Guo Wei died, and his adopted son, Prince of Jin Chai Rong, succeeded him.
units.literal: That month Zhou ruler Wei died; his adopted son, Prince of Jin Chai Rong, succeeded to the throne.

units.zh: 是月，周主榮殂，子宗訓立。
units.en: That month Zhou's ruler Rong died and his son Zongxun succeeded to the throne.
units.literal: That month, Zhou's ruler Rong died and his son Zongxun succeeded to the throne.

units.zh: 戊戌，遣前復州防禦使吳巒權知貝州軍事，詔節度使王令溫赴闕。
units.en: On wuxu former Fu defense commissioner Wu Luan was sent to act as Bei's military administrator, and commissioner Wang Lingwen was ordered to court.
units.literal: On wuxu, the former defense commissioner of Fuzhou, Wu Luan, was dispatched to act as administrator of Beizhou's military affairs; an edict ordered military commissioner Wang Lingwen to come to court.

units.zh: 癸丑，詔河陽節度使符彥卿、宋州節度使高行周、貝州節度使王令溫、同州節度使李承福、陳州梁漢璋、亳州李萼、懷州薛懷讓並赴闕，分命使臣諸州郡巡檢，以契丹入寇故也。
units.en: On guichou an edict summoned commissioners Fu Yanqing of Heyang, Gao Xingzhou of Song, Wang Lingwen of Bei, Li Chenfu of Tong, Liang Hanzhang of Chen, Li E of Bo, and Xue Huairang of Huai to court and dispatched envoys to inspect the prefectures, because the Khitan had invaded.
units.literal: On guichou, an edict ordered military commissioners Fu Yanqing of Heyang, Gao Xingzhou of Songzhou, Wang Lingwen of Beizhou, Li Chenfu of Tongzhou, Liang Hanzhang of Chenzhou, Li E of Bozhou, and Xue Huairang of Huaizhou all to come to court; envoys were separately appointed to inspect the various prefectures and commanderies, because the Khitan had entered to raid.

units.zh: 庚午，以權知北京軍府事、汾州刺史符彥超為晉州留後，以前陳州刺史劉伸殷為陝州留後。
units.en: On gengwu, Fu Yanchao, acting administrator of the Northern Capital Military Prefecture and prefect of Fenzhou, was made acting military commissioner of Jinzhou; Liu Shenyin, former prefect of Chenzhou, was made acting military commissioner of Shanzhou.
units.literal: On gengwu, acting Beiping military commissioner and Fenzhou prefect Fu Yanchao was made Jinzhou acting military commissioner; former Chenzhou prefect Liu Shenyin was made Shanzhou acting military commissioner.

units.zh: 甲寅，以晉州留後符彥超為北京留守，以鎮州副使王建立為鎮州留後，以右龍武統軍安崇阮為晉州留後。
units.en: On jiayin Fu Yanchao became Beijing regent; Wang Jianli became Zhen acting commissioner; An Chongruan became Jin acting commissioner.
units.literal: On jiayin, Jin acting commissioner Fu Yanchao was made Beijing regent; Zhenzhou deputy Wang Jianli was made Zhen acting commissioner; Right Dragon Martial commander An Chongruan was made Jin acting commissioner.

units.zh: 以汝州防禦使趙延壽為河陽節度使，以比部郎中、知制誥劉讚為中書舍人，以河陽掌書記程遜為比部員外郎、知制誥，以代州刺史李德充為蔚州刺史。
units.en: Zhao Yanshou, Ru defense commissioner, became Heyang commissioner; Liu Zan, Bureau of Revenue director and edict drafter, became Secretariat drafting officer; Cheng Xun, Heyang secretary, became Bureau of Revenue vice director and edict drafter; Li Dechong of Dai became Yu prefect.
units.literal: Ruzhou defense commissioner Zhao Yanshou was made Heyang military commissioner; Bureau of Revenue director and edict drafter Liu Zan was made Secretariat drafting officer; Heyang secretary Cheng Xun was made Bureau of Revenue vice director and edict drafter; Dai prefect Li Dechong was made Yu prefect.

units.zh: 時李嗣源總帳下親軍攻東北隅；
units.en: Li Siyuan led the household guard against the northeast corner;
units.literal: Li Siyuan commanded the personal troops below the tent attacking the northeast corner;

units.zh: 李嗣源壞夾城東北隅，率先掩擊，梁軍大恐，南向而奔，投戈委甲，噎塞行路，斬萬餘級，獲其將副招討使符道昭洎大將三百人，芻粟百萬。
units.en: Li Siyuan breached Jiacity's northeast and charged in; Liang panicked and fled south, shedding arms until the road jammed; over ten thousand were killed; Fu Daozhao and three hundred officers were taken, with a million bundles of fodder.
units.literal: Li Siyuan broke the northeast corner of Jiacity and led the assault; the Liang army was greatly terrified and fled south, casting weapons and armor; the road was choked; more than ten thousand were beheaded; deputy pacification commissioner Fu Daozhao and three hundred great generals were captured, and a million measures of fodder.

units.zh: 五月辛未朔，晨霧晦暝，帝率親軍伏三垂崗下。
units.en: At the xinwei new moon in the fifth month, thick morning fog hid Cunxu's personal troops below Sanchui Ridge.
units.literal: On the first day xinwei of the fifth month, morning fog dark and dim, the Emperor led his personal army in ambush below Sanchui Ridge.

units.zh: 丙辰，以秘書監呂琦為禮部侍郎，歸德軍節度使趙在禮改天平軍節度使，昭義軍節度使兼侍衛親軍馬步軍都虞候杜重威改忠武軍節度使，忠武軍節度使、侍衛親軍馬步軍都指揮使劉知遠改歸德軍節度使，前河陽節度使兼奉國左右廂都指揮使侯益改昭義軍節度使。
units.en: On bingchen Lü Qi, palace library director, became vice minister of rites; Zhao Zaili of Guide became Tianping military commissioner; Du Chongwei of Zhaoyi became Zhongwu military commissioner; Liu Zhiyuan of Zhongwu became Guide military commissioner; and Hou Yi, former Heyang commissioner, became Zhaoyi military commissioner.
units.literal: On bingchen, Lü Qi, Director of the Palace Library, was appointed Vice Minister of Rites; Zhao Zaili, Military Commissioner of the Guide Army, was changed to Military Commissioner of the Tianping Army; Du Chongwei, Military Commissioner of Zhaoyi and Chief Adjutant of the Palace Guard Horse and Foot, was changed to Military Commissioner of the Zhongwu Army; Liu Zhiyuan, Military Commissioner of the Zhongwu Army and Commander-in-Chief of the Palace Guard Horse and Foot, was changed to Military Commissioner of the Guide Army; Hou Yi, former Military Commissioner of Heyang and Commander of the Left and Right Wings of the Fengguo Army, was changed to Military Commissioner of Zhaoyi.

units.zh: 九月乙己，樞密使郭威檢校太師、兼侍中，宋州節度使兼侍衛親軍都指揮使史宏肇加兼中書令。
units.en: In the ninth month, on the yisi day, the Bureau of Military Affairs commissioner Guo Wei was made Acting Grand Tutor and concurrent Palace Attendant, and the Song Prefecture military governor and concurrent commander of the Imperial Guards Shi Hongzhao was given the additional title of Grand Councilor.
units.literal: In the ninth month, on the yisi day, the Bureau of Military Affairs commissioner Guo Wei was made Acting Grand Tutor and concurrent Palace Attendant; the Song Prefecture military governor and concurrent commander of the Imperial Guards Shi Hongzhao was given the additional title of Grand Councilor.

units.zh: 帝然之，於是宏肇與宰相、樞密使、三司使，次第加恩。
units.en: The emperor approved, and then Hongzhao, the chief ministers, the Bureau of Military Affairs commissioner, and the Commissioner of the Three Departments received favors in sequence.
units.literal: The Emperor approved, and then Hongzhao, the chief ministers, the Bureau of Military Affairs commissioner, and the Commissioner of the Three Departments received favors in sequence.

units.zh: 李式、翟光鄴為樞密使，王景崇為宣徽使，餘官各有署置。
units.en: Li Shi and Zhai Guangye were made commissioners of the Bureau of Military Affairs, Wang Jingchong palace commissioner, and the remaining posts were each filled.
units.literal: Li Shi and Zhai Guangye were made commissioners of the Bureau of Military Affairs, Wang Jingchong was made palace commissioner, and the remaining offices were each filled.

units.zh: 丙子，以金部郎中、知制誥馮玉為檢校尚書右僕射，充潁州團練使。
units.en: On bingzi Feng Yu, a bureau director in the Ministry of Revenue and edict drafter, was made acting Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and regimental commissioner of Ying Prefecture.
units.literal: On bingzi, Feng Yu, bureau director in the Ministry of Revenue and drafter of edicts, was made acting Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and filled the post of regimental commissioner of Yingzhou.

units.zh: 辛巳，西面軍前奏，今月十三日，階州刺史王宏贄、瀘州刺史馮暉，自利州取山路出劍門關外倒下，殺敗董璋守關兵士三千餘人，收復劍州。
units.en: On xinsi the western front reported: on the thirteenth Jie prefect Wang Hongzan and Lu prefect Feng Hui, from Li by a mountain path outside Jianmen Pass, struck Dong Zhang's garrison of more than three thousand and recovered Jian.
units.literal: On xinsi the western-front army reported: on the thirteenth of this month Jie prefect Wang Hongzan and Lu prefect Feng Hui, from Li by a mountain path outside Jianmen Pass, came down upon Dong Zhang's garrison of more than three thousand and recovered Jian prefecture.

units.zh: 父景珂，倜儻有膽氣。
units.en: His father Jing Ke was bold and daring by nature.
units.literal: His father Jing Ke was bold and free-spirited and had courage.

units.zh: 翟光鄴，字化基，濮州鄄城人。
units.en: Di Guangye, whose style name was Huaji, came from Juancheng in Puzhou.
units.literal: Di Guangye, style name Huaji, was a native of Juancheng in Puzhou.

units.zh: 梁貞明初，唐莊宗始駐軍於河上，景珂率聚邑人守永定驛，固守逾年，後為北軍所攻，景珂戰歿，眾潰。
units.en: In the first year of Liang Zhenming, Zhuangzong of Tang first encamped his army on the Yellow River; Jing Ke led the people of his district to hold Yongding Post, held firm for more than a year, was later attacked by the northern army, fell in battle, and his force broke.
units.literal: In the first year of Zhenming of Liang, Tang Zhuangzong first stationed his army on the Yellow River; Jing Ke led the people of his district to hold Yongding Post, defended it for more than a year, and was later attacked by the northern army; Jing Ke died in battle and the host scattered.

units.zh: 戊子，晉州藥元福、滑州白重贊、相州王進、同州張鐸並加檢校太傅；
units.en: On wuzi Yao Yuanfu of Jinzhou, Bai Chongzan of Huazhou, Wang Jin of Xiangzhou, and Zhang Duo of Tongzhou were all made acting grand mentors;
units.literal: On wuzi, Yao Yuanfu of Jinzhou, Bai Chongzan of Huazhou, Wang Jin of Xiangzhou, and Zhang Duo of Tongzhou were all made Acting Grand Mentor;

units.zh: 以蕃漢兵馬都孔目官郭威為權樞密使、檢校司徒；
units.en: Guo Wei was made acting Commissioner of Military Affairs and Acting Minister of Works;
units.literal: Guo Wei, chief clerk of tribal and Han forces, was made acting Commissioner of Military Affairs and Acting Minister of Works;

units.zh: 是日，定州孫方簡、徐州劉赟並加同平章事，以利州節度使宋延渥為滑州節度使。
units.en: That day, Sun Fangjian of Ding Prefecture and Liu Yun of Xuzhou were both made Grand Councilors, and the Lizhou military governor Song Yanwo was appointed military governor of Hua Prefecture.
units.literal: That day, Ding Prefecture Sun Fangjian and Xuzhou Liu Yun were both made Grand Councilors; the Lizhou military governor Song Yanwo was made military governor of Hua Prefecture.

units.zh: 丙寅，以西面行營馬軍都指揮使、檢校太保、鄭州刺史、充本州防禦使王彥章為檢校太傅。
units.en: On bingyin, Wang Yanzhang, Western Line horse commander, honorary Grand Guardian, and Zheng prefect and defense commissioner, was promoted to honorary Grand Mentor.
units.literal: On bingyin, Western Line camp horse commander, honorary Grand Guardian, Zheng prefect, and Zheng defense commissioner Wang Yanzhang was made honorary Grand Mentor.

units.zh: 十二月，晉王自太原復至魏州。
units.en: In the twelfth month the Prince of Jin returned from Taiyuan to Weizhou.
units.literal: In the twelfth month the Prince of Jin came again from Taiyuan to Weizhou.

units.zh: 定州留後孫行友、邢州留後田景鹹、陜州留後韓通、靈武留後馮繼業並正授節度使。
units.en: Acting commissioners Sun Xingyou of Dingzhou, Tian Jingxian of Xingzhou, Han Tong of Shaanzhou, and Feng Jiye of Lingwu were all formally appointed military governors.
units.literal: Sun Xingyou, acting commissioner of Dingzhou; Tian Jingxian of Xingzhou; Han Tong of Shaanzhou; and Feng Jiye of Lingwu were all formally appointed military governors.

units.zh: 潞州節度使、充河中一行副都署常思加檢校太師；
units.en: the Lu Prefecture military governor and concurrent deputy commander of the Hezhong campaign Chang Si was given the additional title of Acting Grand Preceptor;
units.literal: the Lu Prefecture military governor and concurrent deputy commander of the Hezhong campaign Chang Si was given the additional title of Acting Grand Preceptor;

units.zh: 乙亥，以侍衛馬軍都指揮使李彥韜權知侍衛司事。
units.en: On yihai Li Yantao, commander of the Imperial Guard cavalry, was placed in acting charge of the Imperial Guard bureau.
units.literal: On yihai Li Yantao, commander of the Imperial Guard horse army, was made acting head of the Imperial Guard bureau.

units.zh: 是夜，偵知張彥澤已至滑州，召李崧、馮玉、李彥韜入內計事，方議詔河東劉知遠起兵赴難，至五鼓初，張彥澤引蕃騎入京。
units.en: That night scouts reported Zhang Yanzhe at Huazhou; Li Song, Feng Yu, and Li Yantao were called in to deliberate and were debating an edict for Liu Zhiyuan of Hedong to march to the rescue when at the fifth watch Zhang Yanzhe led Khitan cavalry into the capital.
units.literal: That night scouts learned Zhang Yanzhe had reached Huazhou; Li Song, Feng Yu, and Li Yantao were summoned within to plan; they were just discussing an edict for Liu Zhiyuan of Hedong to raise troops to the rescue when at the first watch of the fifth drum Zhang Yanzhe led barbarian cavalry into the capital.

units.zh: 宰臣趙瑩、樞密使馮玉、侍衛馬軍都指揮使李彥韜隨帝入蕃，契丹主遣三百騎援送而去。
units.en: Grand Counsellor Zhao Ying, Commissioner Feng Yu, and Li Yantao, commander of the Imperial Guard cavalry, accompanied the emperor into Khitan territory while the Khitan lord sent three hundred horsemen as escort.
units.literal: Grand Counsellor Zhao Ying, Commissioner Feng Yu, and Li Yantao, commander of the Imperial Guard horse army, followed the Emperor into the barbarians; the Khitan lord sent three hundred cavalry to escort and send them off.

units.zh: 偽命鳳州節度使王承捷、故鎮屯駐指揮使唐景思次第迎降，得兵一萬二千、軍儲四十萬。
units.en: Shu-appointed Fengzhou commissioner Wang Chengjie and former garrison commander Tang Jingsi surrendered in turn, yielding twelve thousand men and four hundred thousand in stores.
units.literal: The Shu-appointed Fengzhou military commissioner Wang Chengjie and the former garrison commander Tang Jingsi in succession came to surrender; they gained twelve thousand troops and four hundred thousand in military stores.

units.zh: 丙申，潞州小校楊立據城叛，以李嗣源為招討使，陝州留後李紹真為副，率師以討之。
units.en: On bingshen Yang Li, a Luzhou junior officer, rebelled and held the city; Li Siyuan was made pacification commissioner with Li Shaozhen of Shanzhou as deputy to march against him.
units.literal: On bingshen, Luzhou junior officer Yang Li seized the city in rebellion; Li Siyuan was made pacification commissioner, Shaanzhou acting commissioner Li Shaozhen deputy, and they led troops to attack him.
